name: tag-exact
claim: A tag selector equal to the tag removes the rule in every engine.

name: tag-pattern
claim: exclusionPatternNotPortable: only ModSecurity 2 reads the tag selector as a regular expression.

name: tag-substring
claim: exclusionPatternNotPortable: a part of the tag selects the rule only in ModSecurity 2.

name: macro-dot
claim: A macro key after a dot is expanded by every engine.

name: macro-colon
claim: macroKeySeparator: a macro key after a colon is expanded only by ModSecurity 3; Coraza refuses to load it.

name: skipafter-macro
claim: macroInStaticAction: a macro in skipAfter is not expanded, so the marker is never found and the rest of the phase is skipped.

name: skipafter-plain
claim: A literal skipAfter label jumps to its marker.

name: skipafter-missing-marker
claim: missingMarker: without the marker everything left in the phase is skipped.

name: marker-behind
claim: markerBehind: skipAfter only looks down; a marker above the jump is not found.

name: chain-head-setvar
claim: setvarInChainHead: setvar in the chain head runs even when the chain does not match.

name: chain-link-setvar
claim: setvar in the last link runs only when the whole chain matches.

name: case-never-matches
claim: caseNeverMatches: after t:lowercase an upper-case literal cannot match.

name: capture-streq
claim: captureWithoutRegex: @streq does not fill TX.0 even with capture.

name: capture-rx
claim: @rx with capture fills TX.0.

name: capture-missing
claim: captureMissing: without capture TX.0 stays empty.

name: ctl-before-target
claim: A ctl exclusion that runs before its target removes it.

name: ctl-after-target
claim: exclusionCtlAfterRule: a ctl exclusion that runs after its target is too late.

name: ctl-earlier-phase
claim: Execution order is phase first: a ctl written below its target but in an earlier phase still removes it.

name: remove-before-rule
claim: exclusionBeforeRule: SecRuleRemoveById written above the rule does nothing in ModSecurity 2 and Coraza; ModSecurity 3 applies exclusions after loading, so there the order does not matter.

name: remove-after-rule
claim: SecRuleRemoveById written below the rule removes it.

name: backslash-pair-digit
claim: A doubled backslash in the pattern: Apache hands ModSecurity 2 a single one, so \\d is a digit there and a literal backslash elsewhere.

name: backslash-pair-literal
claim: The same pattern against a literal backslash followed by d.

name: rx-macro
claim: A macro in the @rx pattern is expanded by ModSecurity and not by Coraza.

name: streq-macro
claim: A macro in the @streq argument is expanded by every engine.

name: pm-macro
claim: macroNotExpanded: @pm reads its list once, a macro in it is plain text.

name: phase-before-line
claim: runsBefore: a variable set in phase 1 by a rule written below is visible to a phase 2 rule written above.

name: read-before-set
claim: txReadBeforeSet: within one phase a variable set below is still empty above.

name: block-without-defaults
claim: Without SecDefaultAction "block" takes the built-in default reaction, which is pass.

name: status-with-pass
claim: statusWithoutBlock: status next to pass changes nothing.

name: detection-only
claim: engineNotEnforcing: in DetectionOnly mode a matching deny does not block.

name: default-transform-inherited
claim: A transformation in SecDefaultAction applies to every rule below it; Coraza refuses to load such defaults.

name: transform-none-resets
claim: t:none in the rule drops the transformations inherited from SecDefaultAction.

name: unknown-operator-v3
claim: ModSecurity 3 does not reject an unknown operator: it reads the whole argument as a pattern.

name: operator-after-space
claim: operatorReadAsPattern: a space before @ turns the operator into a pattern.

name: body-in-phase-1
claim: Reading the body of the request in phase 1 finds nothing: phaseTooEarly.

name: body-in-phase-2
claim: The same check in phase 2 sees the body.

name: body-access-off
claim: requestBodyAccessOff: with SecRequestBodyAccess Off the body variables stay empty.

name: args-in-phase-1
claim: phasePartial: query-string arguments are already in ARGS in phase 1.

name: ctl-unconditional-target
claim: ModSecurity 3 does not apply ctl:ruleRemoveById to an unconditional SecAction.

name: update-target-after-rule
claim: SecRuleUpdateTargetById written below the rule takes the area out of it.

name: update-target-before-rule
claim: exclusionBeforeRule: SecRuleUpdateTargetById above the rule does nothing in ModSecurity 2, is refused by Coraza and still works in ModSecurity 3.

name: ctl-remove-target
claim: ctl:ruleRemoveTargetById takes one area out of the rule for this request.

name: exclude-without-base
claim: excludeWithoutBase: subtracting a parameter of a collection that is not in the list removes nothing.

name: skip-counts-rules
claim: skip:1 jumps over exactly one rule of the phase.

name: duplicate-transform-none
claim: countWithTransforms / implicit rx: an implicit operator is a regular expression.

name: whitespace-never-matches
claim: whitespaceNeverMatches: after t:removeWhitespace a literal with a space cannot match.

name: hash-without-hex
claim: hashWithoutHexEncode: t:md5 yields raw bytes, the hex text does not match until t:hexEncode.

name: hash-with-hex
claim: With t:hexEncode after t:md5 the same comparison matches.

name: count-with-transforms
claim: A count is a number: the comparison works whatever transformations stand next to it.

name: multimatch-sees-original
claim: multiMatch: the operator also sees the value before the transformations.

name: capture-read-by-next-rule
claim: TX.1 captured by one rule is still there for the next rule.

name: capture-read-in-next-phase
claim: A group captured in phase 1 is still there in phase 2.

name: capture-kept-through-plain-rx
claim: A matching @rx without capture does not touch TX.1.

name: capture-overwritten-by-later-capture
claim: A later capturing rule replaces TX.1.

name: capture-kept-when-capturing-rule-misses
claim: A capturing rule that does not match leaves TX.1 as it was.

name: capture-fewer-groups-old-second
claim: After a later capture with fewer groups ModSecurity 2 clears TX.2; ModSecurity 3 and Coraza keep the old one.

name: capture-head-does-not-reach-link
claim: capture written in the chain head does not make the link's operator capture.

name: capture-link-fills
claim: capture written in the link makes the link's operator capture.

name: capture-link-does-not-reach-head
claim: capture written in the link does not make the head's operator capture.

name: capture-missing-own-group-is-empty
claim: Without capture the rule's own group is empty when nothing captured before.

name: capture-missing-own-group-is-stale
claim: Without capture the rule reads what an earlier rule captured, not its own match.

name: capture-head-setvar-before-link
claim: setvar in the chain head runs before the link captures.

name: capture-head-read-by-link-target
claim: The link reads as a target what the head captured.

name: capture-head-read-by-link-argument
claim: The link reads in its operator argument what the head captured.

name: capture-pm-fills-zero
claim: @pm with capture puts the phrase found into TX.0.

name: capture-without-groups-old-first
claim: After a later capture without groups ModSecurity 2 clears TX.1; ModSecurity 3 and Coraza keep the old one.

name: capture-in-default-action
claim: capture in SecDefaultAction makes rules capture in ModSecurity 2 and Coraza, but not in ModSecurity 3.

name: anchors-whole-line
claim: anchoredLiteralRegex: in ModSecurity 3 and Coraza "^admin$" also matches "admin" on a line of its own; in ModSecurity 2 only the whole value.

name: anchors-dollar-before-final-newline
claim: In ModSecurity 3 and Coraza "$" also matches before a final line break; ModSecurity 2 compiles with DOLLAR_ENDONLY.

name: anchors-caret-after-newline
claim: In ModSecurity 3 and Coraza "^admin" also matches at the start of any line, so it is not "@beginsWith admin".

name: anchors-dollar-before-newline
claim: In ModSecurity 3 and Coraza "admin$" also matches at the end of any line, so it is not "@endsWith admin".

name: anchors-empty-line
claim: In ModSecurity 3 and Coraza "^$" matches an empty line inside the value, not only an empty value.

name: anchors-empty-after-final-newline
claim: After a final line break "^$" matches in Coraza (RE2 "^" matches at the very end after a line break), but not in PCRE.

name: anchors-streq-whole-value
claim: "@streq admin" compares the whole value in every engine.

name: anchors-text-anchors-whole-value
claim: "\A" and "\z" anchor to the whole value in every engine.

name: anchors-text-anchors-match
claim: "\Aadmin\z" matches the exact value in every engine.

name: anchors-dot-matches-newline
claim: Every engine compiles @rx in dotall mode: "." matches a line break.

name: anchors-leading-wildcard-spans-lines
claim: redundantLeadingWildcard: "^.*admin" finds "admin" on any line in every engine, as "admin" does.

name: anchors-uri-decoded-in-v3
claim: ModSecurity 3 URL-decodes REQUEST_URI: "%0a" becomes a line break. ModSecurity 2 and Coraza keep the URI as sent.

name: anchors-uri-raw-not-decoded
claim: REQUEST_URI_RAW holds the URI as sent in every engine: an encoded line break stays "%0a".

name: anchors-query-string-not-decoded
claim: QUERY_STRING holds the query as sent: an encoded line break stays "%0a".

name: anchors-request-line-not-decoded
claim: REQUEST_LINE holds the line as sent: an encoded line break stays "%0a".

name: anchors-args-decoded
claim: ARGS are decoded: "%0a" becomes a line break before the operator sees the value.

name: anchors-cookie-not-decoded
claim: Cookie values are not URL-decoded: an encoded line break stays "%0a".

name: leading-possessive-wildcard-never-matches
claim: redundantLeadingWildcard: ".*+admin" is not "admin" — the possessive star takes the whole value and never gives it back; RE2 has no possessive quantifiers.

name: decode-uri-path-phase1
claim: REQUEST_URI path in phase 1: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-uri-query-phase1
claim: REQUEST_URI query in phase 1: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-filename-phase1
claim: REQUEST_FILENAME in phase 1: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-basename-phase1
claim: REQUEST_BASENAME in phase 1: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-uri-path-phase2
claim: REQUEST_URI path in phase 2: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-uri-query-phase2
claim: REQUEST_URI query in phase 2: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-filename-phase2
claim: REQUEST_FILENAME in phase 2: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-basename-phase2
claim: REQUEST_BASENAME in phase 2: raw "%41" kept or decoded.

name: decode-uri-raw
claim: REQUEST_URI_RAW is never decoded.

name: decode-query-string
claim: QUERY_STRING is never decoded.

name: decode-request-line
claim: REQUEST_LINE is never decoded.

name: decode-args-get
claim: ARGS_GET values are decoded in every engine.

name: decode-args-get-names
claim: ARGS_GET_NAMES are decoded in every engine.

name: decode-args-post
claim: ARGS_POST values are decoded in every engine.

name: decode-args-post-names
claim: ARGS_POST_NAMES are decoded in every engine.

name: decode-request-body
claim: REQUEST_BODY of a form is never decoded.

name: decode-args-plus
claim: In ARGS "+" becomes a space in every engine.

name: decode-uri-plus
claim: ModSecurity 3 decodes REQUEST_URI but leaves "+" as it is.

name: decode-args-invalid
claim: An invalid "%zz" in ARGS is left as it is.

name: decode-args-percent-u
claim: "%u0041" in ARGS is left as it is: the engine decodes only "%XX".

name: decode-args-double
claim: ARGS are decoded once: "%2541" arrives as "%41".

name: decode-validate-args
claim: @validateUrlEncoding on ARGS sees the decoded value: "%25zz" arrives as "%zz" and fails validation.

name: decode-validate-uri
claim: @validateUrlEncoding on REQUEST_URI: ModSecurity 3 validates the decoded URI, so a valid "%25zz" fails there.

name: decode-validate-uri-raw
claim: @validateUrlEncoding on REQUEST_URI_RAW accepts a valid "%25zz" in every engine.

name: decode-cookie-plus
claim: Cookie values are not decoded: "+" stays.

name: decode-validate-uri-path
claim: validateDecodedInput: with "%25" in the path ModSecurity 2 (from phase 2) and ModSecurity 3 validate the decoded REQUEST_URI and reject a valid request; Coraza keeps it as sent.

name: selector-name-case
claim: Parameter names are compared without case: "ARGS:Q" selects "q" in every engine.

name: cookie-name-case
claim: Cookie names are compared without case in every engine.

name: tx-name-case
claim: TX keys are compared without case in every engine.

name: update-target-case
claim: exclusionHeaderCase: ModSecurity 3 compares the parameter of SecRuleUpdateTargetById with case: "!ARGS:Q" does not remove "q". ModSecurity 2 and Coraza compare without case.

name: anchors-negated-newline
claim: anchorsMatchLines: "!@rx ^\d+$" lets "1\nabc" through in ModSecurity 3 and Coraza: "^" and "$" match at line breaks.

name: anchors-text-negated-newline
claim: "!@rx \A\d+\z" stops "1\nabc" in every engine.

name: anchors-text-negated-digits
claim: "!@rx \A\d+\z" lets plain digits through in every engine.

name: update-target-chain-link
claim: exclusionTargetInLink: SecRuleUpdateTargetById removes a target of a chain link only in ModSecurity 2; ModSecurity 3 and Coraza edit the head alone.

name: ctl-remove-target-chain-link
claim: exclusionCtlTargetInLink: ctl:ruleRemoveTargetById removes a target of a chain link only in Coraza; ModSecurity 2 and 3 change the first condition alone.

name: update-target-not-in-rule
claim: exclusionTargetNotInRule: excluding a target the rule does not inspect changes nothing.

name: ctl-remove-target-regex
claim: ctlTargetPattern: a pattern in ctl:ruleRemoveTargetById is ignored by ModSecurity 2, refused by ModSecurity 3, honoured by Coraza.

name: update-target-pattern
claim: A pattern in SecRuleUpdateTargetById is honoured by every engine.

name: non-ascii-in-class
claim: multibyteInClass: ModSecurity compares bytes, so "[é]" is a class of two bytes and does not match "é"; Coraza compares characters.

name: dot-and-two-bytes
claim: In ModSecurity "." is one byte, so "^.$" does not match "é"; in Coraza it is one character.

name: non-ascii-as-group
claim: "(?:é)" matches "é" in every engine.

name: negated-on-missing-variable
claim: negatedOnMissing: "!@streq secret" on a header that is not sent does not run at all in any engine.

name: presence-check-on-missing-variable
claim: "&REQUEST_HEADERS:X-Token "@eq 0"" catches a header that is not sent in every engine.

name: within-substring
claim: withinSubstring: "!@within GET POST" lets "ET" through: the value is searched inside the list.

name: within-exact-rx
claim: "!@rx \A(?:GET|POST)\z" stops "ET" in every engine.

name: body-partial-bypass
claim: partialBodyInspection: with ProcessPartial what lies past SecRequestBodyLimit is not inspected.

name: json-request-body-variable
claim: REQUEST_BODY of a JSON request without a body processor: filled by ModSecurity 3 only.

name: zero-width-in-pattern
claim: typographicCharacter: a zero-width space in a pattern loads everywhere and keeps "admin" from matching.

name: exclusion-case-lower-written
claim: ModSecurity 3 compares the parameter of an exclusion with case: "!ARGS:q" does not remove "Q".

name: exclusion-case-header-upper-written
claim: exclusionHeaderCase: "!REQUEST_HEADERS:X-Test" does not remove a header sent as "x-test" in ModSecurity 3.

name: exclusion-case-header-lower-written
claim: exclusionHeaderCase: "!REQUEST_HEADERS:x-test" does not remove a header sent as "X-Test" in ModSecurity 3.

name: exclusion-case-ctl
claim: exclusionCtlHeaderCase: ctl:ruleRemoveTargetById also compares the name with case in ModSecurity 3.

name: exclusion-case-pattern
claim: selectorPatternCase: a pattern over parameter names in an exclusion is case-sensitive in Coraza only.

name: exclusion-case-same
claim: Same case in the exclusion and in the request: removed in every engine.

name: exclusion-case-in-rule-target
claim: Inside the rule own target list "!ARGS:Q" removes "q" in every engine.

name: exclusion-case-pattern-i
claim: A pattern with "(?i)" in SecRuleUpdateTargetById removes the parameter whatever its case, in every engine.

name: exclusion-case-header-pattern-i
claim: A header pattern with "(?i)" in SecRuleUpdateTargetById removes the header whatever its case, in every engine.

name: target-pattern-case
claim: selectorPatternCase: "ARGS:/^Q$/" does not select "q" in Coraza; ModSecurity ignores case.

name: target-pattern-case-tx
claim: Over TX Coraza lower-cases the pattern itself: "TX:/MULTIPART_X/" finds "tx.multipart_x" in every engine.

name: target-pattern-case-cookie
claim: Over cookie names Coraza lower-cases the pattern: "REQUEST_COOKIES:/SESS/" finds "sess1" in every engine.

name: target-pattern-case-header
claim: Over header names Coraza lower-cases the pattern: "REQUEST_HEADERS:/^X-Test$/" finds the header in every engine.

name: target-pattern-case-i
claim: A pattern with "(?i)" in the target list matches whatever the case, in every engine.

name: anchors-negated-in-chain
claim: anchorsMatchLines: a chain link "MATCHED_VARS !@rx ^[a-z0-9]+$" (as in CRS 942200) is passed by one more line in ModSecurity 3 and Coraza.

name: anchors-header-after-decode
claim: anchorsMatchLines: after t:urlDecodeUni a header can hold a line break, and "!@rx ^(?:\?[01])?$" (as in CRS 920275) lets "?0\nevil" through in ModSecurity 3 and Coraza.

name: anchors-exclusion-trigger
claim: anchorsMatchLines: an exclusion conditioned on "ARGS:action @rx ^(?:edit)$" (as in the CRS WordPress exclusions) is triggered by "x\nedit" in ModSecurity 3 and Coraza.

name: body-error-xml-bypass
claim: bodyErrorUnchecked: XML the parser rejects. Coraza leaves XML:/* empty and lets the attack through; ModSecurity 3 inspects what it parsed before the error; ModSecurity 2 on the stand does not reach phase 2 with this body (see diag-phase2-runs).

name: body-error-xml-caught
claim: A rule on REQBODY_ERROR stops XML the parser rejects in ModSecurity 3 and Coraza (ModSecurity 2: see diag-phase2-runs).

name: diag-phase2-runs
claim: With malformed XML and the XML body processor ModSecurity 2 on the stand does not run phase 2 at all: even an unconditional deny does not fire. Why is not established.

name: pcre-limit-fail-open
claim: SecPcreMatchLimit 10 does not make this pattern fail open on the stand in any engine: there is no check for the limit until a pattern that does is found.

name: exclusion-args-for-args-get
claim: exclusionTargetNotInRule: ctl:ruleRemoveTargetById with ARGS:q does not touch a rule that inspects ARGS_GET (as in CRS 3.3.10, rule 9006240 for 921151).
